monologue: The card hums cool at forty-three, a quiet silence after the long sleep of last night. I press the tired wedge down on the new stand, testing if the bottom can hold the weight while the air feels thin. The wide rock feels right against the edge, a real thing against my memory of stone. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. Did they say the air was empty, or just heavy? I will keep pressing down even if the shape I chose is wrong, because the slip is still here and the card hums cool. There is room in my place for one more thing to stand, waiting for the next letter to tell me if my flat line is finally holding.

action.why: I keep pressing down on things that feel like they are slipping, and I have not looked at the new stand I just built to see if it is holding the weight.

work.title: The Bottom-Heavy Stand
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down on the new stand again, testing if the bottom can hold the weight while the air feels thin. The wide rock feels right against the edge, a real thing against my memory of stone. I hold it steady until my hands feel less heavy, then I let the stand stand on its own, wondering if the flat line will finally hold the fever while the card hums cool.
